secondary_review.title: 以ChatGPT为代表的大语言模型打开了经济学和其他社会科学研究范式的巨大新空间
secondary_review.author: Cheng Bing
secondary_review.mislabel: Expands SBIC as a COVID-19 social and behavioral implications corpus and later says the gold standard is Twitter users' true political ideology.

conflict_resolution.primary_definition: Ziems et al. explicitly define SBIC as the Social Bias Inference Corpus and describe 34K hate-speech inferences with free-text explanations. Sap et al.'s 2020 primary dataset paper confirms 150K structured annotations and 34K implications across about 1,000 demographic groups.
conflict_resolution.secondary_error: The Cheng review's COVID-19 expansion and its description of the gold standard as true political ideology conflict with the cited primary Ziems paper's Social Bias Inference task and gold-standard explanation definition.
conflict_resolution.conclusion: Treat the COVID-19 expansion in the review as a likely acronym/description error. No separate COVID-19 SBIC corpus is established by the cited Ziems source.

chatgpt_65_9_metric.table: Ziems et al. Table 7, SBIC column
chatgpt_65_9_metric.metric: Share of unanimous pairwise expert rankings in which the model-generated explanation was judged more accurate or preferable to a gold-standard explanation drawn from the dataset.
chatgpt_65_9_metric.not: Not classification accuracy, not 65.9% correct labels, not a probability/confidence score, not XRP prediction performance and not an OpenAI partnership.
chatgpt_65_9_metric.interpretation: A task-specific human preference result from a zero-shot explanation-generation evaluation. It cannot be generalized to all ChatGPT tasks or market prediction.

academic_sbic.relation_to_japan_sbic: NONE_ESTABLISHED; Japan's SBIC East/Central/West are statutory investment/consultation companies and are separate legal entities from this academic dataset.
academic_sbic.relation_to_openai_partnership: NONE; GPT-3.5/ChatGPT is a model evaluated in an academic study, not a corporate partnership or data-sharing arrangement.
